before.known: I met a few friends and then went out
before.target: mačiau keletą draugų, o paskui išėjau į lauką

after.known: I saw a few friends and then went out

problem: Meaning: 'met' is translated by 'mačiau' (saw).
evidence: U04 uses 'saw a few friends' for the same 'mačiau keletą draugų'; 'sutikau' is not taught until seed 234.

before.known: he went out to tell me something important
before.target: jis išėjau į lauką man pasakyti ką nors

problem: Grammar: 'išėjau' is first person but the subject is 'he'. 'important' is also missing from the target.
evidence: Known 'he went out to tell me something important' => 'jis išėjau į lauką man pasakyti ką nors'.

before.known: tell me what he wants
before.target: man pasakyti, ko nori

problem: Mood mismatch: the known is an imperative, the target is a bare infinitive.
evidence: 'tell me what he wants' => 'man pasakyti, ko nori'.

before.known: they told us he will ask you about it
before.target: jie mums pasakė, kad jis tavęs paklaus

problem: Meaning: the known 'about it' is missing from the target.
evidence: Target 'jie mums pasakė, kad jis tavęs paklaus' has no equivalent of 'about it'.

before.known: just now they asked
before.target: ką tik jis tavęs paklaus

problem: Meaning: the known is 'they asked' (past), but the target is 'jis tavęs paklaus' (he will ask you).
evidence: Known 'just now they asked' => 'ką tik jis tavęs paklaus'.

before.known: he just asked you something
before.target: ką tik jis tavęs paklaus ką nors

problem: Tense: the known is past 'asked', but the target 'paklaus' is future.
evidence: 'he just asked you something' => 'ką tik jis tavęs paklaus ką nors'.

before.known: he just told me something important
before.target: ką tik jis man pasakė ką nors

problem: Meaning: 'important' is missing from the target.
evidence: 'he just told me something important' => 'ką tik jis man pasakė ką nors'.

before.known: he would ask you if he could speak to us
before.target: jis tavęs paklaus, jei galėtų kalbėti su mumis

problem: Mood: 'would ask' is translated by the future 'paklaus'.
evidence: 'he would ask you if he could speak to us' => 'jis tavęs paklaus, jei galėtų kalbėti su mumis'.

before.known: he would give you more if he could speak better
before.target: jis tau duotų daugiau, jei galėtų kalbėti

problem: Meaning: 'better' is missing from the target.
evidence: 'if he could speak better' => 'jei galėtų kalbėti'.

before.known: he tried to tell me the answer
before.target: jis bando man pasakyti atsakymą

problem: Tense: the known 'tried' is past, but the target 'bando' is present.
evidence: 'he tried to tell me the answer' => 'jis bando man pasakyti atsakymą'.

before.known: he would give you the answer if you asked him
before.target: jis tau duotų atsakymą, jei paprašyčiau tavęs

problem: Person: 'if you asked him' is translated as 'jei paprašyčiau tavęs' (if I asked you).
evidence: Known 'he would give you the answer if you asked him'.

before.known: I know a young man who just asked for help
before.target: pažįstu jauną vyrą, kuris ką tik norėjo pagalbos

problem: Meaning: the known 'just asked for help' is translated as 'ką tik norėjo pagalbos' (just wanted help).
evidence: 'pažįstu jauną vyrą, kuris ką tik norėjo pagalbos'.

before.known: a woman who started
before.target: ta moteris, kuri pradėjo

problem: Meaning: 'a woman' is translated as 'ta moteris' (that woman). It is also a fragment.
evidence: Known 'a woman who started' => 'ta moteris, kuri pradėjo'.

before.known: a woman who would help you if she could
before.target: ta moteris, kuri tau padėtų, jei galėtų

problem: Meaning: 'a woman' is translated as 'ta moteris' (that woman). It is also a fragment, not a complete USE sentence.
evidence: 'a woman who would help you if she could' => 'ta moteris, kuri tau padėtų, jei galėtų'.

before.known: a woman who told me something new
before.target: ta moteris, kuri man pasakė ką nors naujo

problem: Meaning: 'a woman' is translated as 'ta moteris'. It is also a fragment, not a complete USE sentence.
evidence: Sibling rows U01-U05 all use 'a woman' => 'ta moteris'.

before.known: a woman who can remember the answer
before.target: ta moteris, kuri gali prisiminti atsakymą

problem: Meaning: 'a woman' is translated as 'ta moteris'. It is also a fragment, not a complete USE sentence.
evidence: 'a woman who can remember the answer' => 'ta moteris, kuri gali prisiminti atsakymą'.

before.known: a woman who is trying to speak Lithuanian
before.target: ta moteris, kuri bando kalbėti lietuviškai

problem: Meaning: 'a woman' is translated as 'ta moteris'. It is also a fragment, not a complete USE sentence.
evidence: 'a woman who is trying to speak Lithuanian' => 'ta moteris, kuri bando kalbėti lietuviškai'.

before.known: a woman who just started to work with us
before.target: ta moteris, kuri ką tik pradėjo dirbti su mumis

problem: Meaning: 'a woman' is translated as 'ta moteris'. It is also a fragment, not a complete USE sentence.
evidence: 'a woman who just started to work with us' => 'ta moteris, kuri ką tik pradėjo dirbti su mumis'.

before.known: I know your sister wants to work with you
before.target: pažįstu tavo seserį, kuri nori dirbti su tavimi

problem: Meaning: the known 'I know your sister wants to work' is translated as a relative clause, 'your sister, who wants'.
evidence: 'pažįstu tavo seserį, kuri nori dirbti su tavimi' adds a relative clause the known does not have.

before.known: I know someone who knows your brother
before.target: pažįstu žmogų, kuris pažįsta tavo broliu

after.known: I know someone who works with your brother
after.target: pažįstu žmogų, kuris dirba su tavo broliu

problem: Grammar: 'tavo broliu' (instrumental) is used as the object of 'pažįsta'.
evidence: 'kuris pažįsta tavo broliu' needs the accusative; 'broliu' is only correct after 'su'.

before.known: I met your brother last night and he told me something
before.target: vakar vakare sutikau tavo broliu ir man pasakė ką nors

problem: Grammar: 'sutikau tavo broliu' puts the instrumental where the accusative is needed. The verb 'pasakė' also has no subject.
evidence: 'vakar vakare sutikau tavo broliu ir man pasakė ką nors'.

before.known: I met your brother last night who said that he wants to speak
before.target: vakar vakare sutikau tavo broliu, kuris pasakė, kad nori kalbėti

problem: Grammar: 'sutikau tavo broliu' puts the instrumental where the accusative is needed.
evidence: 'vakar vakare sutikau tavo broliu, kuris pasakė, kad nori kalbėti'.

before.known: I need to work before the weekend
before.target: mums reikia dirbti prieš savaitgalį

after.known: we need to work before the weekend

problem: Meaning: the known has 'I', but the target 'mums reikia' means 'we need'.
evidence: 'I need to work before the weekend' => 'mums reikia dirbti prieš savaitgalį'.

before.known: my father likes to read something new
before.target: mano tėvui mėgsta skaityti ką nors naujo

problem: Grammar: the dative 'mano tėvui' is used with the nominative-subject verb 'mėgsta'.
evidence: 'mano tėvui mėgsta skaityti ką nors naujo' needs 'mano tėvas'.

before.known: my father likes to speak Lithuanian
before.target: mano tėvui mėgsta kalbėti lietuviškai

problem: Grammar: the dative 'mano tėvui' is used with the nominative-subject verb 'mėgsta'.
evidence: 'mano tėvui mėgsta kalbėti lietuviškai'.

before.known: my father likes to work together
before.target: mano tėvui mėgsta dirbti kartu

problem: Grammar: the dative 'mano tėvui' is used with the nominative-subject verb 'mėgsta'.
evidence: 'mano tėvui mėgsta dirbti kartu'.

before.known: it doesn't please me to spend more time on this
before.target: man nepatinka skirti daugiau laiko

problem: Meaning: 'on this' is missing from the target.
evidence: 'to spend more time on this' => 'skirti daugiau laiko'.
